text:
elena: Heads up — new egress policy hit prod-az2 ~2m ago, observed a handful of GPU nodes stuck in 'joining'.
matt: Saw that, +1. Logs show keystore proxy TLS handshakes failing: 
```
ERROR keystore: dial tcp 10.15.2.8:443: i/o timeout
TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: handshake failure
```
jia: Looks like firewall SNI inspection was rolled in yesterday evening change. Might be dropping ALPN or SNI for keystore host.
elena: @infra-oncall can you confirm firewall rule id? We need a quick exception. :pray:
infra-oncall: Rule fw-egress-sni-tightening (rev 12) — we tightened to block non-sni whitelisted hosts to reduce audit data exfil. I can open a 30m exception for `keystore.redwood.internal` now.
matt: Please do. This is preventing nodes from fetching boot keys; warm pools are draining.
sre-bot: Deploy alert: gpu-warmup-rate < 50% for prod-az2. Autoretry scheduled in 5m.
keystore-bot: Keystore queue: decrypt latency spike -> 500ms+; pending requests 342 -> risk of evictions.
elena: Temporary exception is fine, but we need root cause — is it SNI or the added deep-inspect TLS proxy?
jia: Packet captures show TLS ClientHello missing SNI when old cuda-agent v0.9.2 talks to keystore proxy. The proxy rejects connection if SNI absent.
elena: So older agents are non-SNI, firewall was fine before. New rule now denies them. Options: 1) add host-based exception; 2) roll a tiny agent patch adding SNI; 3) fallback keystore route (non-inspected path).
matt: Short-term: host-based exception for `keystore.*` + route to pass-through proxy to unblock onboarding. Mid-term: agent patch.
infra-oncall: Exception in place for 30m -> confirm pass-through route update done. Can you verify node joins?
jia: Node join rate recovered to normal within 90s. Warm pool back to expected capacity. :tada:
elena: Nice. Now follow-ups: we need an audit-impact assessment. The rule was introduced to reduce audit noise but this exception weakens it. Any metrics?
matt: Audit log volume for egress TLS dropped ~18% after rule, but keystore traffic was small (0.6%). Exception increases cost negligibly, but risk is SNI-less agents still on older versions.
sre-bot: FYI natgw conntrack had spike ~+40% during failed handshakes, close to threshold; could be churn/cost when many nodes retry.
elia: (typo) meant elena: We should gate exception behind a canary with stricter logging. Proposal: 1) ship agent v0.9.3 with SNI by EOD to canary region; 2) keep host exception only in prod-az2 until canary completes; 3) lower audit sampling for non-keystore hosts to compensate cost for 24h.
matt: Agree. Also recommend a keystore healthcheck endpoint that doesn't require TLS full handshake for warming nodes (short-term token bootstrap endpoint over internal-only path).
infra-oncall: I'll open a ticket and set retention/alert: if natgw-conntrack > 85% hold, rollback rule.
keystore-bot: Scheduled job: rotate ephemeral certs for internal keystore in 2h — note this may bump TLS handshakes.
jia: Good catch — coordinate rotate after agent patch to avoid additional failures.
elena: I'll draft runbook changes: add known_hosts exception flow, node-version detection during warmup, and an opt-in fast-path for pre-auth on first join.
matt: Also add cost estimate: temporary exception + 24h reduced sampling ~+$120/day in log egress costs for prod region. Not huge.
sre-bot: Incident note: mitigated; root cause = SNI-less agents + stricter SNI/firewall policy. Follow-up tickets: AGENT-472 (SNI patch), FW-889 (audit policy tuning), KEE-131 (keystore bootstrap endpoint).
elena: Thanks everyone. I'll post a summary in #eng-platform and tag compliance for audit implications. :white_check_mark:
